item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: 682 isn't a mindless, ravenous cosmic force. It's a conscious being motivated to destroy us because it finds us unbearably revolting. WE are "The Thing(s) that Should not be", in it's perception, and it's desire to eradicate us is, in context, perfectly reasonable. It's also a mutating, adapting, regenerating monster, not some sort of metaphysical Galactus. I'd no-vote it as a nonspecific tale, it depends a bit too much on cadence and not enough on content, but as a 682 piece it's a huge -1.

It elevates it beyond the original concept (which was great to begin with) without contradicting established not-canon.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's a good tale about something, but I'm not sure if it's about 682. Mostly because the lizard just isn't that effective. Sure, he can kill hundreds of thousands, maybe even millions or billions, and no force we could ever bring to bear would do more than slow him down. It would be horrible, and civilization as we know it may well collapse in the aftermath. But one monster, no matter how vicious and unkillable, just can't wipe out all life on Earth. And what's with him turning into a black hole? I don't think 682 has ever gone on record as hating the stars themselves.

There is no canon, and all that. But this is just incompatible with the 682 we know and cower in abject terror of.

item.content:encoded:
"SCP-682 appears to have a hatred of all life"
I thought that if it hates everything it would probably go about killing everything around it. Given that it needs some form of energy to survive, some of that killing is bound to involve consumption. Since it is able to adapt to most anything, it should be able to reconfigure itself to consume most materials. Of course, it probably wouldn't be able to adapt to heat-death. Not much you can do once that happens. I do see your point though.
